answer: Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a orchard index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Because the cedar index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the shale audit republishes the digest set at close. Filling 30 aliases as a result needs 30 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
